title: On-call & Incident Response - Comprehensive Runbook (2026)
author: Samira Patel
content:
Summary:
This document is Redwood Inference's canonical, comprehensive runbook for on-call operations and incident response. It consolidates the incident lifecycle, severity definitions, runbooks for common failure modes, postmortem process and template, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer communication templates for our status page. The intent is to provide an actionable single-page reference for responders and engineers during incidents and for managers running game days and post-incident reviews.

Scope:
- Applies to all production-facing Redwood services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private control plane, and Redwood Console).
- Covers Sev 0-3 incidents, runbook steps, escalation paths, and post-incident procedures.
- Excludes development-only issues and non-prod environments unless explicitly invoked by SRE.

Key definitions and severity matrix:
1. Severity levels (owner: eng-sre):
   - Sev 0 (P0) - Total outage or data loss impacting >=50% of customer traffic or severe security incident.
     - Target response: 5 minutes.
     - Pager escalation: page SRE lead and engineering manager.
   - Sev 1 (P1) - Service severely degraded (latency > 5x p50, errors > 5% for > 5 minutes) affecting critical customers.
     - Target response: 15 minutes.
   - Sev 2 (P2) - Partial degradation or feature impact (errors between 1-5% or isolated region issues).
     - Target response: 60 minutes.
   - Sev 3 (P3) - Minor issues, non-critical bugs, or customer-reported nuisances.
     - Target response: next business day triage.

Roles & responsibilities:
- First responder (on-call engineer): Triage, begin investigation, apply immediate mitigations, and update Status Page.
- SRE lead / incident commander (IC): Coordinate cross-team activity, make decisions on mitigations/fallbacks and timeout-based escalations.
- Service owner: Provide domain knowledge and approve rollbacks/config changes.
- Communications lead (support or SRE): Draft and publish customer-facing updates and internal incident notes.
- Postmortem owner: Compile write-up, assign action items, and track remediation to closure.

Incident lifecycle (high-level procedure):
1. Detection: Alert fired, pager triggered.
2. Initial acknowledgement: First responder acknowledges within target window and posts initial status in incident channel (#inc-<service>-<id>).
3. Triage & classification: Determine severity, impacted customers, and immediate risk.
4. Mitigation & containment: Apply runbook steps or safe mitigations (traffic routing, feature flags, restart nodes).
5. Recovery & verify: Restore service and validate with synthetic traffic and customer checks.
6. Communication: Update status page, support tickets, and internal stakeholders with cadence.
7. Post-incident review: Write postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and publish final with action items tracked to completion.

Practical runbooks (select common scenarios):
- High error-rate (5xx > 5% for API):
  1. Identify onset time and scope: check Grafana dashboard api/errors and logging cluster for error spike.
  2. Confirm deploy activity in last 30 minutes (CI/CD): `gitlab-ci pipeline list --project redwood/service-api --last 5` and check release notes.
  3. If errors correspond to new deploy: roll back to previous stable tag with `kubectl rollout undo deployment/service-api -n prod`.
  4. If unrelated to deploy: enable traffic throttling and circuit-breakers via routing plane (console -> routing -> throttles) and scale replicas: `kubectl scale deployment/service-api --replicas=+2 -n prod` or increase Dedicated capacity as allowed.
  5. Monitor: target error-rate <1% sustained for 10 minutes before removing throttles.

- High latency (p95 > target or latency > 5x baseline):
  1. Check CPU/GPU saturation: dashboards -> gpu-fleet-and-capacity and node exporter metrics.
  2. Inspect batching and KV cache hit-rate: runtime-metrics/kvcache_hit_rate.
  3. Apply mitigations: reduce request concurrency for affected route, enable fallback lighter-weight model (model routing policy), or increase batch size where safe.
  4. If hardware issue suspected, cordon affected node and migrate pods: `kubectl cordon <node>` and `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets`.

- Deployment-caused failures:
  1. Halt rollout: `kubectl rollout pause` and revert to last stable.
  2. Open pipeline and capture failed step logs.
  3. If canary failed: disable canary and re-run tests locally with representative load.

Escalation path and paging policy:
- Pager rotates to on-call SRE; if not acknowledged within 15 minutes for Sev0/1 escalate to SRE lead and service owner.
- Email escalation: after 30 minutes with no resolution for Sev0/1, notify exec on-call list and Customer Success.

Status page and customer communications (templates):
- Status page best practices:
  - Update at incident start, every 30 minutes for Sev0/1, and on major milestones (mitigation, partial restore, full restore, postmortem published).
  - Use concise language: impact, affected regions, workarounds, ETA.

- Template: Initial status (short):
  "We are investigating issues affecting [service name]. Users may experience increased error rates or timeouts. Our engineers are actively investigating. Impacted regions: [region list]. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."

- Template: Update (mitigation applied):
  "Mitigation in place: We have applied [mitigation] and are seeing partial improvement. Error rate has decreased from X% to Y% over the last 10 minutes. Customers may still see degraded performance; no data loss detected. Next update in 30 minutes or when status changes."

- Template: Resolved:
  "Resolved: The incident impacting [service] has been resolved at [time UTC]. Root cause: [brief summary]. Postmortem (draft) will be published within 72 hours and final report with action items will follow. We apologize for the disruption."

Postmortem process and minimum template (owner: Postmortem owner):
- Timeline: create draft within 72 hours, share with reviewers within 7 days, publish final within 14 days.
- Required sections for every postmortem:
  - Title, Sev, Start/End times (UTC), Impact summary (customers, revenue, SLOs affected), What happened (sequence), Root cause, Mitigations applied, Corrective actions (owner + ETA), Detection and alerting gaps, Lessons learned, Rollout/QA changes, Links to logs/dashboards.
- Postmortem example header (text):
  "Title: Sev 1 - Hosted API High Error Rate - 2026-02-03
   Start: 2026-02-03T13:04:00Z
   End: 2026-02-03T14:42:00Z
   Impact: ~18% of requests returned 5xx, affecting hosted API for NA region."

On-call rotations and rules (owner: eng-sre manager):
- Primary on-call shift: 24/7 rotation, 1-week primary shifts. Secondary on-call (escalation) covers weekdays 08:00-18:00 for additional capacity.
- On-call playbook highlights:
  - Hand-off: update runbook notes, ensure handover in #ops-handoffs Slack thread, confirm access to runbooks and keys.
  - Quiet hours & paging: follow paging schedule in PagerDuty; non-urgent issues should be filed as tickets.
  - Compensation & time-off policy: see People Ops handbook for on-call pay and backup rules.

Game days and readiness exercises:
- Objective: validate runbooks, exercise cross-team coordination, verify alarms and SLO alert thresholds, and measure mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to restore (MTTR).
- Cadence: quarterly game days per product area; each game day must have a scenario doc, facilitator (SRE lead), observers, and a blameless retrospective.
- Example scenario: Simulate a model-serving node failure that causes increased latency in a single region; exercises: traffic failover, model routing to lighter quantized variant, and customer-facing status update.

Runbook maintenance and ownership:
- Every service runbook must list the primary owner, backup owner, and last-reviewed date.
- Runbooks are reviewed quarterly and after any Sev0/1 incident.
- PR process: create PR to confluence runbook folder and request reviewer from eng-sre and service team.

Operational tooling & dashboards (quick links):
- Primary dashboards: Grafana -> API Errors, Latency by route, GPU Fleet utilization, KV Cache hit-rate.
- Log search: Kibana -> queries: `service:service-api AND level:ERROR AND @timestamp:[now-15m TO now]`
- Pager/On-call: PagerDuty -> Redwood On-call; IRC/Slack: #inc-<service>-<id> channels auto-created by PagerDuty.

SLOs and alert thresholds (sample table):
- service-api: 99.9% availability (monthly), alert if availability < 99.95% in 1-hr rolling window.
- hosted-inference-route: p95 latency target 250ms, alert if p95 > 500ms for 10 minutes.

Checklist for responders (quick actions):
1. Acknowledge alert and create incident channel.
2. Post initial status and severity classification.
3. Capture scope (region, customer impact, start time).
4. Follow relevant runbook and apply safe mitigations.
5. Escalate if no improvement per SLA.
6. Prepare status page message and cadence.

Tracking and remediation of action items:
- Action items from postmortems must be tracked in the engineering tracker with owner, priority, and ETA. SRE manager reviews open items weekly until closure.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets:
- Rollback deployment: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/service-api -n prod`
- Scale deployment: `kubectl scale deployment/service-api --replicas=5 -n prod`
- Check recent deploys: `gitlab-ci pipeline list --project redwood/service-api --last 10`
- Drain node: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Contacts and escalation lists (owners):
- SRE Pager: pagerduty@redwood.example.com
- Engineering Manager on-call: eng-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Exec on-call: exec-oncall@redwood.example.com

Revision history:
- 2026-02-10: Initial draft (Samira Patel)
- 2026-02-18: Added templates and escalations (Ethan Garcia)
- 2026-03-01: Final review and publish (Lena Wu)

This runbook is intended to be a living document. If you find gaps during an incident or game day, create a post-incident action and update the runbook immediately.
